name: Ouroboros Energy Resonant Carrier Lantern
description: The Resonant Carrier Lantern exploits low-frequency electromagnetic bleed from Ouroboros Energy's own municipal power grid infrastructure, piggybacking encrypted data packets onto the 50-60Hz carrier waves that saturate every district of GLMZ. By modulating signal phase differentials at the sub-milliamp level, it creates a covert communication channel that is effectively invisible to conventional spectrum sweeps — the signal looks, to any monitoring system, like ordinary grid noise. The device itself is housed in a weathered industrial casing roughly the size of a thermos, designed to blend into maintenance corridors, junction boxes, and utility tunnels without drawing inspection.

specifications.range: Up to 3km along connected grid infrastructure
specifications.encryption: 128-bit rolling phase cipher, re-keyed every 90 seconds
specifications.power_draw: Parasitic — draws from host grid, no internal battery required
specifications.simultaneous_channels: Up to 4 paired units per carrier frequency

tactical_use: Operators plant Lanterns at accessible power conduit junctions — inside elevator shafts, beneath street-level transformer housings, or within building utility closets — creating a semi-permanent covert channel that persists as long as the grid is live. Because the signal rides existing infrastructure rather than broadcasting through open air, it bypasses most airborne signal detection suites entirely. Field teams use paired Lanterns as dead-drop relay points, leaving time-delayed messages that recipients retrieve hours later without ever making live contact. The primary vulnerability is physical discovery of the device itself.
cultural_context: Among GLMZ's sprawling underclass of infrastructure workers, electricians, and tunnel-runners, the Lantern has acquired an almost folkloric reputation. Ouroboros Energy's grid is omnipresent — it powers the corpo towers, the slum blocks, the black-market fabricators — and the idea of using the company's own veins to whisper secrets past its eyes carries a particular satisfaction. Union organizers in the Outer Wards were among the earliest adopters, and the device is still sometimes called 'the Organizer's Wire' in those communities. For corporate security divisions, the Lantern represents a persistent headache: the channel is nearly undetectable without physically auditing every conduit coupling in a district.
known_users: Mid-tier fixers with established safe house networks
Grid maintenance workers moonlighting as couriers
story_hooks: A Lantern unit recovered from a demolished substation still has active messages queued — messages dated three weeks after the building's listed demolition date.
Ouroboros Energy's internal security division quietly offers off-books bounties for recovered Lanterns, suggesting they contain something more than just comms capability.
A fixer's entire dead-drop network goes dark simultaneously �� every Lantern on the chain silent. Either someone found them all, or the grid segment they relied on was deliberately cut.
A street electrician offers to install a Lantern for the players, but her rate is suspiciously low — and she wants a copy of every message routed through it.
related_entities: Ouroboros Energy Power Distribution Trunk Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cylindrical device resembling a heavy-duty industrial thermos or signal relay unit. Its form is deliberately nondescript—designed to vanish visually among utility infrastructure. The casing has a robust, field-worn appearance suggesting years in maintenance corridors and junction boxes.
physical_description.dimensions: 18cm tall, 7cm diameter cylindrical form — roughly thermos-sized, easily concealable in a tool bag or mounted horizontally in a utility conduit
physical_description.weight_description: 410g; handheld and portable, comfortable to carry for extended periods or position in fixed locations. Light enough for one-handed placement, substantial enough to feel engineered
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum alloy body with industrial-grade polymer collar bands at top and base. Designed for harsh environments and repeated handling
physical_description.finish: Brushed matte aluminum with intentional weathering — micro-scratches, faint oxidation marks, and dull patina suggest legitimate field use. Not pristine; authenticity through wear
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with charcoal polymer accent bands. Minimal branding to avoid visual attention. Subtle copper-oxide discoloration near the base where grid interface contacts show age
physical_description.interface_elements: Three recessed stainless steel contact points arranged in a triangular pattern on the base for grid coupling. A single amber LED indicator (dim, barely visible unless active) recessed into the upper collar. No visible screens or keypads — all configuration is wireless or requires a paired handheld device. A sealed maintenance port with a non-standard five-pin connector hidden under a spring-clip cover
distinctive_features: Grid coupling base with three heavy-duty contact points designed to bridge utility infrastructure without requiring permanent installation
Subtle phase-modulation indicator LED that pulses at frequencies matching internal encryption key rotation
Shielded ferrite ring near the midsection, visually apparent as a slightly darker band with subtle lattice texture
Cable management loop molded into the polymer collar for securing the device to conduit or mounting brackets
Micro-etched serial number and regulatory compliance marks deliberately worn to near-illegibility, suggesting field authenticity
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ouroboros Energy corporate logo (circular snake motif) stamped small and high on the body, barely prominent. OUROBOROS ENERGY text in small sans-serif font. Regulatory stamp for GLMZ infrastructure compliance with date codes faded to suggest age. No marketing—purely functional labeling
physical_description.condition_typical: Seen mounted horizontally in junction boxes or clamped to utility conduit runs. When in operation, the amber indicator glows faintly in sync with power grid harmonics. Dust and mineral deposits accumulate naturally on the contact points. The device is never truly 'off'—it draws parasitically, making it virtually undetectable in an active electrical environment
